skill.description: Generates hosted images through Luxin's zero-setup CLI, with a no-spend guide, budget caps, recoverable jobs, receipts, and durable media URLs.
skill.summary: Create hosted AI images with Luxin while checking readiness and estimated spend first.
skill.author: agentspace-so

security_audit.summary: The supplied static catalog primarily matches Markdown formatting, documentation URLs, example placeholders, and model-selection prose rather than executable code. The actual skill nevertheless instructs operators to run unpinned npx packages with automatic confirmation, creating a material third-party package execution boundary. Its hosted workflow may send prompts to Luxin and can incur media charges when an operator allows spending.

remediation.issue: Runtime examples execute luxin-cli@latest through npx with automatic confirmation.
remediation.suggestion: Pin the CLI to a reviewed version, publish integrity information, and require an explicit operator confirmation before installation or execution.

remediation.issue: Image creation can spend hosted credits and process prompt content remotely.
remediation.suggestion: Show estimated cost, retention details, and a clear consent step before any non-guide generation command.

remediation.issue: The global skill-install examples can change agent configuration and filesystem state.
remediation.suggestion: Offer a workspace-local installation as the default and explain every path and configuration change before running it.

content.user_title: Create Hosted AI Images with Luxin
content.value_statement: Hosted image generation often requires separate provider accounts, credentials, and billing setup. This skill guides Luxin image creation with readiness checks, budget limits, job recovery, and receipts.
actual_capabilities: Starts a no-spend readiness guide before image generation.
Creates hosted images with the Luxin CLI and a selected model.
Sets an estimated per-image spending limit in the documented runtime command.
Uses recoverable jobs, durable media URLs, and cost receipts described by the shared Luxin contract.
Installs the intent skill for Codex through the documented skills.sh command.
limitations: Requires network access and the external Luxin CLI.
Creates images in a hosted service rather than on the local machine.
Generation can consume hosted credits when media spending is allowed.
Model availability, prices, policies, and output quality can change outside this skill.

use_cases.title: Explore product concepts
use_cases.description: Create a first visual direction after confirming readiness and a per-image budget limit.

use_cases.title: Prepare campaign illustrations
use_cases.description: Generate durable hosted artwork and retain job and cost information for later review.

use_cases.title: Prototype agent workflows
use_cases.description: Use the no-spend guide to validate a hosted image path before allowing paid generation.

prompt_templates.title: Generate a first concept
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the no-spend guide for a [subject] image. If it is ready and spending is allowed, create a [style] image with a maximum estimated cost of [amount].

prompt_templates.title: Create a product image
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a hosted image of [product] for [audience]. Use [composition], [lighting], and [background]. Keep the estimated cost per image at or below [amount].

prompt_templates.title: Produce campaign art
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a [format] campaign illustration for [campaign]. Include [subject], [visual style], and [brand colors]. Report the job reference and cost receipt.

prompt_templates.title: Build a controlled generation flow
prompt_templates.prompt: First run the Luxin no-spend guide for [brief]. Only if it reports ready and spending is approved, create [number] images using [model]. Return durable media URLs, job details, and costs.

output_examples.input: Create a compact field camera on a stainless workbench. Check readiness first and limit estimated cost to $0.07.
output_examples.output: The readiness guide is checked before creation. If approved, the hosted image request uses the stated cost cap and returns a recoverable job and durable media URL.

output_examples.input: Generate a clean product concept for a reusable water bottle campaign.
output_examples.output: The request becomes a hosted product-image job with a clear subject, campaign context, and a cost record for review.

output_examples.input: Validate an image workflow without spending credits.
output_examples.output: The no-spend guide identifies missing inputs or returns a safe recommended command instead of generating media.

best_practices: Run the no-spend guide before creating media or allowing any charge.
Set an estimated cost limit and confirm approval before each paid generation.
Review hosted service privacy, retention, and billing terms before sending sensitive prompts.
anti_patterns: Do not run unpinned npx commands without reviewing the package source and version.
Do not send confidential prompts or protected visual material to a hosted service without authorization.
Do not enable paid generation when the readiness guide reports missing inputs or spending is not approved.

faq.question: Does this skill generate images locally?
faq.answer: No. It uses Luxin as a hosted runtime and requires network access.

faq.question: Do I need a provider API key?
faq.answer: The documentation describes a zero-setup hosted workflow and does not require a user-supplied provider API key.

faq.question: How can I avoid spending credits?
faq.answer: Start with the documented no-spend guide and use its recommended safe command when it is not ready to create.

faq.question: Can I control estimated cost?
faq.answer: Yes. The main runtime example includes a maximum estimated cost per image parameter.

faq.question: What should I save after generation?
faq.answer: Keep the durable media URL, recoverable job information, and cost receipt described by the shared contract.

faq.question: Is installation safe to run automatically?
faq.answer: Review the package and pin a version first. The documented npx commands use @latest with automatic confirmation.
